cyber.title: Iran-linked intrusions into US water controllers
cyber.method: Attackers changed settings on internet-facing PLCs.
cyber.summary: Science Times reports intrusions into water systems in at least 12 states. The FBI says attackers changed controller settings; there has been no widespread loss of supply.

actor.name: CyberAv3ngers (IRGC-linked) (claimed); officials call Iran a suspect, not confir

sources.text: Science Times reports attacks on US water systems across at least 12 states; the FBI says attackers changed settings on internet-facing PLCs, officials call Iran a suspect, not confirmed, with no widespread supply loss.
NBC News reported on Sept 2, citing four sources, that Iranian hackers also tried to reach US telecom and energy systems. The attempts were reported as unsuccessful so far.
CSIS's incident list says the IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers claimed the August water campaign across at least a dozen states. It says the US government had not publicly attributed it.

ABC News reported on Aug 4, citing sources, that water-sector intrusions reached at least 12 states, with Iran the prime suspect. Involvement was unconfirmed and supplies saw no widespread disruption.

TechCrunch reports an updated advisory from the FBI, NSA, DOE and CISA. It says Iranian actors target controllers from Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens. Those products are also used in the US.

Separately, US outlets report that Radical Numerics is testing local pathogen screening with a model called Omnii-1.
items.why: If AI meaningfully helps someone design or make a dangerous pathogen, a single misuse could cause mass casualties. Screening tools are one proposed defence.
items.who: A former Google AI safety researcher (warning); Radical Numerics (screening test)

items.title: Japan weighs penalties for AI firms over safety risks
items.what: Kyodo News and Yonhap report that Japan is considering legislation with AI safety obligations and penalties for companies that violate them. This adds to Australia's planned AI safety regulator and New York's incident-reporting law, which are also in the news.
items.why: Binding safety rules with penalties could make labs report and fix dangerous capabilities faster. Weak or delayed rules leave that to voluntary action.

actions.summary: This window added few new government actions: a reported ASEAN oil-product stockpile, a German gas-reserve bill and a Ukrainian appeal for shelter funding. Most new stories were legal explainers, protests or sport. Taken together, the logged actions point to long-term hedging against supply shocks from the Gulf and against hybrid pressure from Russia, while talks on Ukraine and Iran continue. The preparations are not slowing during those talks, but much of this is scheduled or comes from single sources, so confidence is moderate at best.

patterns.title: Reserve, mobilisation and undersea-protection steps around Russia and NATO's east
patterns.points_to: On both sides, these steps build the ability to grow forces quickly and to guard cables and seabed infrastructure over years. The threat they name is hybrid attack and a possible wider war, not a set date.
patterns.unsaid: Reserve training and Russian reservist recruitment went on through the US-mediated Abu Dhabi talks of 10-12 November. The timing suggests neither side treats the talks as a reason to slow its preparations.
patterns.plain_explanation: Most of these steps follow defence plans and budgets set after 2022, and Russia's BARS reservist drives have run for years. Germany's defence minister says compulsory call-ups are likely unnecessary, which cuts against a near-term surge reading. No new government step was added in this window.

patterns.title: Middle East states ready reserves, shelters and troops while US talks of a deal
patterns.points_to: Together these steps prepare for a longer regional conflict. That could mean missile fire on Israeli and Gulf cities, strained food and fuel imports for Egypt, and a drawn-out Houthi fight with Saudi Arabia.
patterns.unsaid: President Trump said on 10 and 12 November that the war is effectively over and won. Meanwhile Iran threatens US bases, including in Europe, and US aircraft reportedly left a UK base. The gap between the victory talk and these moves suggests governments are hedging against renewed strikes.
patterns.plain_explanation: Israel and the Houthis have been fighting all along, so call-ups and mobilisation rallies may be routine for them. Several items rest on single outlets or on one side's media: Saba for the Houthis, IranWire, and one Romanian outlet for Iraq. Iran's health ministry denies the iodine reports.

patterns.title: Asian importers calm stockpiling fears, then move toward shared oil reserves
patterns.points_to: Energy- and food-importing countries are trying to head off panic buying while shipping through Hormuz faces mines and tanker fires. The reported ASEAN oil-product stockpile shows planning for disruption that could last.
patterns.unsaid: The steps are consistent with governments reassuring the public in the short run while quietly preparing for supply shocks that last longer than they say. Thailand's shift from denial to 72-hour bag advice within a week fits that reading.
patterns.plain_explanation: Southeast Asian energy-security arrangements have been discussed for years, and the stockpile would start in 2027 at the earliest. It is a long-term hedge, not a sign of a specific new threat. The Thai advice may also relate to general disaster preparedness.

patterns.title: 72-hour household kit campaigns spread, mostly on long-set schedules
patterns.points_to: Governments are making a few days of home self-reliance a normal habit for any crisis: storms, power cuts, cyberattacks or war.
patterns.unsaid: The European campaigns run alongside open warnings about Russia, which suggests war is one scenario behind them, though officials frame them as covering all hazards.
patterns.plain_explanation: Most of these follow the EU's 2025 Preparedness Union Strategy or national plans set years ago. Japan, Brazil and Mexico frame their advice around natural disasters. This window brought only more press coverage of UK stockpiling and no new government kit campaign, so the plain explanation covers it.
